articles.title: Jake Paul and Jutta Leerdam unexpectedly grow their family with 15 new babies
articles.summary: Jake Paul and Jutta Leerdam's family just got a whole lot bigger, but definitely not in the way fans might have expected.
articles.body:
Jake Paul and Jutta Leerdam's family just got a whole lot bigger, but definitely not in the way fans might have expected.

The engaged couple shared adorable photos introducing the newest additions to their home: 15 baby goats. Jake and Jutta are surrounded by the tiny animals, holding them, feeding them and clearly enjoying their sudden transformation into goat parents.

And there's something pretty fitting about Jake Paul ending up with a house full of goats. After years of chasing greatness inside the ring, he now has 15 actual GOATs running around at home.

articles.title: Two-time boxing champion Zolani Tete dead at the age of 38 following a terrifying balaclava-clad ambush
articles.standfirst: The boxer was arriving at his residence when he was ambushed by two armed suspects
articles.summary: The boxer was arriving at his residence when he was ambushed by two armed suspects
articles.body:
Former world boxing champion Zolani Tete was killed in a shooting outside his home in South Africa , government officials reported.

Thus, the country's Minister of Sports, Gayton McKenzie, said that Tete, 38, died after being shot in his car, while a 27-year-old woman who was traveling with him in the vehicle is hospitalized after being shot several times.

Tete, who held WBF flyweight world titles between 2007 and 2008 and the WBO bantamweight title in 2017 and 2019 , was waiting for the door to his home to be opened when he was ambushed by two armed suspects.

"The World Boxing Council (WBC) mourned the passing of Zolani Tete. "Our deepest condolences go out to his family, loved ones, and all those who were touched by his extraordinary career," it said on social media.'

According to some local media, Tete was planning to return to the ring in November after serving a four-year ban for doping. The boxer held the record for the fastest "knockout" in a world title fight by defeating fellow South African Gonya 11 seconds into the opening round in the WBO bantamweight world championship.

articles.title: Oscar de la Hoya’s ex-wife walks away with $13.5M property fortune
articles.standfirst: The former boxer and Millie Corretjer finalized their divorce settlement in 2025
articles.summary: The former boxer and Millie Corretjer finalized their divorce settlement in 2025
articles.body:
Oscar De La Hoya's divorce settlement has resulted in a substantial real estate transfer, with his former wife, M ilagros “Millie” Corretjer, receiving full ownership of two properties in Puerto Rico valued at a combined $13.5 million.

According to court documents obtained by TMZ, Corretjer was awarded both properties as part of the former couple's confidential divorce judgment. The latest filing does not alter the terms of their settlement but formally clears the way for the properties to be transferred into Corretjer's name.

The two properties include a residence in San Juan assigned a value of $3.5 million and another property at the Bahia Beach Resort in Rio Grande valued at $10 million. Under the agreement, both properties became Corretjer's sole and separate property, meaning De La Hoya has no remaining claim to either one.

Why the properties were awarded to Millie Corretjer

The court filing was necessary because Puerto Rico requires a certified court order to complete the transfer of real estate following a divorce. The documents therefore provide additional clarity about one part of a settlement whose broader financial terms remain private. De La Hoya and Corretjer finalized their divorce settlement in 2025, ending a marriage that had lasted more than two decades.

Although the couple had been separated for years, their legal divorce process took considerably longer to complete. The $13.5 million in Puerto Rico real estate represents one of the few publicly disclosed elements of their confidential agreement.

A marriage that was always under the spotlight

De la Hoya and Corretjer first met in 2000 and married in October 2001. The couple went on to have three children together: one son and two daughters. Their relationship eventually came to an end, however. The couple separated in 2016, and De la Hoya did not formally file for divorce until January 2023.

The divorce was ultimately settled in 2025, with the remaining terms kept confidential. The latest court filing essentially handles the administrative work necessary to implement the real estate portion of that agreement. The properties awarded to Corretjer add another dimension to the enormous wealth accumulated by De la Hoya during and after his legendary boxing career.

The Mexican American fighter became one of the most recognizable boxers of his generation, winning world titles in six weight classes and earning the nickname “The Golden Boy.” De la Hoya retired from boxing in 2009 with a professional record of 39-6 and 30 knockouts.

His career inside the ring was followed by an equally significant role as a promoter through Golden Boy Promotions, which he founded in 2002. That business helped De la Hoya remain one of the most influential figures in boxing long after his own fighting career ended.

articles.title: Canelo won’t rule out a historic bout at Mexico’s most iconic stadium
articles.standfirst: The proposal generated excitement among boxing fans all over the world
articles.summary: The proposal generated excitement among boxing fans all over the world
articles.body:
S aúl “Canelo” Álvarez has fought in some of the most iconic venues in boxing, from sold-out arenas in Las Vega s to packed stadiums across the globe. Yet one stage remains absent from his remarkable résumé: Mexico City's legendary Estadio Azteca, but t hat could eventually change.

The undisputed Mexican superstar recently revealed that he is open to the possibility of fighting at Estadio Azteca after receiving a public invitation from Emilio Azcárraga, chairman of Televisa and one of the key figures behind the stadium's future plans.

For a fighter who has spent more than a decade carrying the sport's biggest events, the idea of stepping into the ring at one of Mexico's most historic sporting venues appears to hold special significance.

An invitation from one of Mexico's most influential figures

The possibility emerged when Azcárraga discussed his vision for Estadio Azteca following its ongoing modernization efforts. As part of a broader plan to reestablish the venue as a destination for major sporting events, Azcárraga floated the idea of hosting a future Canelo fight at the stadium. He pointed to the rich boxing history associated with the venue and suggested that Álvarez could help usher in a new era for the iconic facility.

The proposal generated excitement among boxing fans. Estadio Azteca has long been considered one of the most important sports venues in the world. Known as the " Colossus of Santa Úrsula," the stadium has hosted World Cup finals, historic soccer matches, and some of the most memorable moments in Mexican sports history. Adding a Canelo Álvarez fight to that list would create another landmark event.

Speaking with TUDN, Álvarez did not dismiss the possibility. Instead, he welcomed it. "For me, it would be an honor, and I'm not ruling it out at all. I hope that one day I get the chance to fight there," Álvarez said. The comments represent the strongest indication yet that boxing's biggest Mexican star would seriously consider bringing one of his future bouts to the famed stadium.

Álvarez also emphasized the unique atmosphere that Estadio Azteca creates, acknowledging the emotional connection millions of Mexican sports fans have with the venue. While no fight has been scheduled and no negotiations have been announced, the fact that Canelo openly embraced the concept has already fueled speculation about what such an event could look like.

A potential career-defining farewell

The idea carries significance beyond a single fight. At 36 years old and already a future Hall of Famer, Álvarez has entered the latter stages of a career that has transformed him into one of the most accomplished fighters in boxing history. A bout at Estadio Azteca could serve as more than just another title defense or pay-per-view attraction. It could become a celebration of his legacy.

For years, many of Canelo's biggest fights have taken place in the United States, where he developed into one of boxing's premier attractions. Returning to Mexico for a major stadium event would give his home-country supporters a rare opportunity to witness one of the sport's biggest stars in an unforgettable setting.

articles.title: Katie Taylor wins her farewell fight in front of 80,000 people
articles.standfirst: One of the greatest female boxers of all time retires at the age of 40 with 26 victories and a single defeat
articles.summary: One of the greatest female boxers of all time retires at the age of 40 with 26 victories and a single defeat
articles.body:
Katie Taylor brought her extraordinary career to an end with a resounding victory over the Frenchwoman Flora Pili, who until yesterday had been unbeaten, in front of 80,000 fans at Croke Park (Dublin) . The Irishwoman, who won Olympic gold when women’s boxing made its debut at London 2012, fulfilled her final wish: to fight in Ireland’s sporting cathedral.

Taylor, 40, dominated her opponent over 10 rounds, earning a unanimous decision victory and retiring as the undisputed 140-pound champion (63.503 kg).

Taylor (26-1) added the vacant WBC super lightweight title to her WBO, WBA, and IBF belts . The judges’ scores were 100-90, 100-90, and 98-91. Pili’s record is 12-1 with this defeat.

" In April 2022, Taylor defeated Amanda Serrano in a packed Madison Square Garden , in what was the first women's boxing match to headline the venue. The two have faced each other three times in total, with Taylor victorious on every occasion, most recently in 2025. That trilogy is the most iconic part of her incredible career.

This latest victory capped an extraordinary journey for Taylor, who began boxing at a time when girls were forbidden from competing as amateurs in Ireland and sometimes took part in bouts simply as "K Taylor".

“Croke Park! We did it! The people of Ireland gave me a dream ending to a dream career. Nothing can top this. Without a doubt, this was the crowning moment of my entire career”

The Irishwoman, who made her professional debut in 2016, retires with 26 victories (6 by KO) and only one defeat , the one suffered against American Chantelle Cameron when moving up to the super lightweight division after having widely dominated the lightweight division.

That happened on May 20, 2023 and just half a year later and at the same venue, Dublin's 3Arena, Taylor got her full revenge.

From the Olympic dream to the dream retirement

After the fight, the Irishwoman placed her gloves in the center of the ring to symbolize her retirement , while her team helped place the belts around them.

After the fight, addressing the euphoric crowd, she said: “Croke Park! We did it! The people of Ireland gave me a dream ending to a dream career. Nothing can top this. Without a doubt, this was the crowning moment of my entire career”.

“ I began my career with the dream of becoming an Olympic champion . I achieved it, but these last 10 years have exceeded my most optimistic expectations. They have been 10 extraordinary years,” Taylor concluded.

articles.title: Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn Prediction: Who is the favorite for this weekend's boxing match?
articles.standfirst: Ryan Garcia will face Conor Benn this Saturday.
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia will face Conor Benn this Saturday.
articles.body:
Next Saturday, September 12, the world of boxing will experience a historic night that promises plenty of excitement when the World Boxing Council (WBC) welterweight world champion, Ryan Garcia , defends his belt for the first time against the dangerous British contender Conor Benn , at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, Nevada.

"García arrives as champion after capturing the WBC welterweight title against Mario Barrios , while Benn will face the biggest opportunity of his career, trying to become a world champion for the first time. Both fighters want to secure the victory to establish themselves in the elite of international boxing.

García will rely on his speed and endurance to retain his world welterweight champion title, while his opponent, a fighter of British origin who is also the son of legendary world champion Nigel Benn , seeks to write his own chapter in the family's boxing history.

Therefore, at MARCA MX we will tell you what the prediction is and everything you need to know about the Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn fight.

What is the prediction for the Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn fight?

Experts and analysts pointed out that this fight will be highly competitive because Benn can make things difficult for any opponent due to his aggressiveness, physical strength, and offensive mindset.

For his part, García has skills such as speed, precision, and counterpunching power to make the difference in this fight, so the current champion is the favorite to win this bout.

Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn: Full card

Here is the full card for this boxing event, which will take place as part of Mexico's Independence Day celebrations:

Main event: Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn

WBC Welterweight World Championship

Co-main event fight: Jai Opetaia vs Noel Mikaelyan

Da’Mazion Vanhouter vs Raphael Akpejiori – Heavyweight

Mark Magsayo vs Andrés Cortés – Lightweight

Oswaldo Molina vs Pablo Rubio

Abel González vs Raúl Salomón

Vlad Panin vs Dakota Linger

José Ramírez vs Alexis Rocha

Sean Garcia vs Abraham Morales

Where to watch the Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn fight?

In Mexico , the Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn fight can be watched live starting at 6:00 p.m. Central Mexico time, through DAZN.

This fight is expected to be intense and give boxing fans plenty to talk about.

articles.title: Canelo Álvarez on Julio César Chávez's feat: “Mexico deserves it, it is the right time”
articles.standfirst: The head of the Council expects an attractive fight card in the country
articles.summary: The head of the Council expects an attractive fight card in the country
articles.body:
A few weeks ago Emilio Azcárraga spoke about the possibility of a Canelo Álvarez fight at the Estadio Azteca , just as happened with Julio César Chávez in 1993 with nearly 133,000 fans in attendance for his victory over Greg Haugen .

For Mauricio Sulaimán , the president of the World Boxing Council , in Mexico it is a good time for an event of that magnitude to take place, due to the passion there is in Mexico for boxing and sports in general, he spoke in EXCLUSIVE for MARCA MX .

Sulaimán, WBC president: “We will always have champions and quality”

Sulaimán, present at the premiere of the new documentary about Julio César Chávez , which premieres on Vix next Friday, September 11, spoke about the quality of Mexican boxing.

“We have William Zepeda , who has just won a world title, Camarón Zepeda, Divino Espinosa . There is a great amount of talent in national boxing, both men and women, and we will always be one of the countries with the greatest number of champions, but above all quality.”

“The boxing serves a great role in society. Both in Mexico and in all countries, every boxer in a gym is a person off the streets where one finds easy ways out for many things, where one can find a wrong path in life,” said the head of the WBC .

Does Canelo Álvarez to the Azteca Stadium?

A few weeks ago Azcárraga said that “ there is an opportunity, for example, I would make a call to Canelo . It would be worth doing one of the fights Canelo has.”

For his part, Saúl Álvarez added that he likes the idea: “it is always an honor to fight in Mexico and in front of my people, even more so in a stadium like the Estadio Azteca , which we all know.”

Sulaimán thinks it is a good time for an event to take place at what is now the Banorte Stadium , but it is not the only historic venue.

“It is necessary, Mexico deserves it, the Mexican fans deserve it. We have, as I was saying, a large number of boxers and above all, being able to have an event, a sellout at the Azteca for Canelo would be wonderful, a carnival of championships at the Plaza de Toros . There have been a great number of highly important fights in our country and I feel that this is the right moment .”

articles.title: How much money does the winner of Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn take home? This is the multimillion-dollar purse for the fight
articles.standfirst: This fight is for the WBC Welterweight World Championship
articles.summary: This fight is for the WBC Welterweight World Championship
articles.body:
The World Boxing Council (WBC) will put the welterweight championship held by Ryan García on the line next Saturday, September 12, against the dangerous Conor Benn in Las Vegas, Nevada, United States. This matchup has sparked a lot of interest among the followers of both pugilists to find out what will happen in the future of the division.

In addition, both boxers' records as professionals are very similar, which suggests it will be a great fight that could go to the judges' decision, since both have amassed 25 victories as professionals, while in defeats Ryan García has two and Conor Benn only one, but now the question is how many millions each fighter will take home in this battle for the WBC Welterweight World Championship.

How much money does the winner of Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn take home?

Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn face off in one of the most compelling bouts in international boxing, with major sporting and financial interests at stake. The fight not only pits two of the division’s most high-profile figures against each other, but also generates substantial revenue through broadcasting on DAZN , PPV sales, and the box office at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas , where ticket sales surpassed $6.3 million on the first day.

As for how much money the winner takes home, there is no official and public figure earmarked exclusively for whoever prevails in the fight. The final amount will depend on the guaranteed purses that Garcia and Benn have negotiated, in addition to their possible shares of the PPV revenue and the gate.

However, various industry reports and rumors have cited guaranteed purses of around $15 million or more for fighters at this level, although these amounts have not been officially confirmed for this bout. Therefore, it is not possible to determine precisely how much money the winner will receive, as the figure could increase depending on the revenue generated by the event.

Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn: Date, time and full card

Next Saturday, September 12, at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas , Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn will face off for the WBC Welterweight Championship in what promises to be an electrifying night with great fights in the ring.

This is the full card for September 12, 2026 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas:

Sean García vs. Abraham Morales - 6 rounds - lightweight

José Ramírez vs Alexis Rocha - 10 rounds - welterweight

Vlad Panin vs Dakota Linger - 6 rounds - super welterweight

Abel González vs Raúl Salomón - 8 rounds - super middleweight

Oswaldo Molina vs Pablo Rubio - 6 rounds - lightweight

Mark Magsayo vs Andrés Cortés - 10 rounds - lightweight

'Da"Mazion Vanhouter vs Raphael Akpejiori - 8 rounds - heavyweight '

Jai Opetaia vs Noel Mikaelian - 12 rounds - cruiserweight

paragraphs: The World Boxing Council (WBC) will put the welterweight championship held by Ryan García on the line next Saturday, September 12, against the dangerous Conor Benn in Las Vegas, Nevada, United States. This matchup has sparked a lot of interest among the followers of both pugilists to find out what will happen in the future of the division.

In addition, both boxers' records as professionals are very similar, which suggests it will be a great fight that could go to the judges' decision, since both have amassed 25 victories as professionals, while in defeats Ryan García has two and Conor Benn only one, but now the question is how many millions each fighter will take home in this battle for the WBC Welterweight World Championship.
How much money does the winner of Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn take home?

Ryan Garcia and Conor Benn face off in one of the most compelling bouts in international boxing, with major sporting and financial interests at stake. The fight not only pits two of the division’s most high-profile figures against each other, but also generates substantial revenue through broadcasting on DAZN , PPV sales, and the box office at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas , where ticket sales surpassed $6.3 million on the first day.

As for how much money the winner takes home, there is no official and public figure earmarked exclusively for whoever prevails in the fight. The final amount will depend on the guaranteed purses that Garcia and Benn have negotiated, in addition to their possible shares of the PPV revenue and the gate.

However, various industry reports and rumors have cited guaranteed purses of around $15 million or more for fighters at this level, although these amounts have not been officially confirmed for this bout. Therefore, it is not possible to determine precisely how much money the winner will receive, as the figure could increase depending on the revenue generated by the event.
